speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing sudden onset abdominal pain; to help me narrow down the cause, please describe the exact location and character of the pain, and if you have any relevant medical history, please share it with me.

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ischemic Bowel (specifically Acute Mesenteric Ischemia or Bowel Infarction) secondary to recent Acute Myocardial Infarction. The patient's age, history of recent MI, sudden onset periumbilical pain, and bloody diarrhea are classic signs of compromised bowel blood flow. Immediate surgical consultation and CT Angiography of the abdomen/pelvis are required to confirm the diagnosis and assess bowel viability.
